# Dutch Bros (BROS) — PE & Earnings Model
**Price:** $64.67 (28 Jul 2026) · **Data:** Q1 FY2026 + FY2025 10-K · **NYSE**

BAU calibrated to management's raised FY2026 guidance ($2.05–2.08bn rev / $370–380m adj. EBITDA). Economic EPS = total NI ÷ total economic shares. Up-C: FY2025 total NI $117.3m, of which $79.8m attributable to Class A.

### PE from earnings ÷ shares (both routes converge)

| Basis | NI | Shares | EPS | PE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reported (Class A) | $79.8m | 125.8m | $0.64 | 101x |
| Economic (total) | $117.3m | 187.7m | $0.625 | 103x |

### BAU net income bridge → shares → EPS ($m unless noted)

| Line | 2025A | 2026E | 2027E | 2028E | 2029E |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Revenue (total)** | 1,638 | 2,055 | 2,555 | 3,133 | 3,784 |
| — Company-operated | 1,509 | 1,918 | 2,410 | 2,980 | 3,621 |
| — Franchise / other | 129 | 136 | 145 | 153 | 163 |
| **Cost of sales** | 1,214 | 1,515 | 1,873 | 2,287 | 2,751 |
| — CoS % of rev | 74.1% | 73.7% | 73.3% | 73.0% | 72.7% |
| **SG&A** | 262 | 277 | 319 | 360 | 397 |
| — SG&A % of rev | 16.0% | 13.5% | 12.5% | 11.5% | 10.5% |
| **EBIT** | 162 | 263 | 363 | 486 | 636 |
| — EBIT margin | 9.9% | 12.8% | 14.2% | 15.5% | 16.8% |
| *(memo) +D&A* | 90 | 112 | 134 | 156 | 178 |
| *(memo) EBITDA* | 252 | 375 | 497 | 642 | 814 |
| Net interest | 28 | 37 | 53 | 69 | 87 |
| Pretax | 134 | 226 | 310 | 417 | 549 |
| Tax @16% | 21 | 36 | 50 | 67 | 88 |
| **Net income (total)** | 113 | 190 | 260 | 350 | 461 |
| Economic shares (m) | 188 | 193 | 199 | 205 | 211 |
| **EPS (economic)** | **$0.60** | **$0.98** | **$1.31** | **$1.71** | **$2.18** |

**What moves the lines:** Revenue is unit-count × AUV (comps +4.5%). **CoS % barely moves** (73–74%) — shop-level costs scale with volume. The earnings leverage is almost entirely **SG&A falling 16.0% → 10.5%** as corporate overhead spreads over 2.3× the revenue → EBIT margin 9.9% → 16.8%. Interest rises as debt-funded new-shop capex builds.

**Shares:** No buyback authorised (thin FCF — all cash into growth). Count **rises ~3%/yr** from two dilutive sources: stock-based comp and Up-C (Class B/LLC-unit) conversions to Class A. So EPS growth trails NI growth by ~3pts/yr. *If* a buyback were introduced (not expected), each ‑1%/yr net share change ≈ +1% EPS.

### Low / High — what changes earnings, costs & PE (vs BAU)

| Driver | LOW | BAU | HIGH | Earnings/cost effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| New shops/yr | 155–170 | 190→235 | 200→270 | Fewer units → less revenue base |
| Comps (SSS) | +2% | +4.5% | +6.5% | Weaker/stronger AUV → drops at ~55% incremental margin |
| SG&A leverage | none (EBITDA ~18% flat) | 18→21% | 18→23.5% | **The swing factor** — no leverage keeps EBIT margin stuck ~10% |
| Rate on debt | 8% | 6.5% | 5% | Higher interest drag on debt-funded builds |
| **→ 2029 EPS** | **$1.16** | **$2.18** | **$3.02** | |
| **→ 2029 PE @ $64.67** | **56x** | **30x** | **21x** | |

**Read:** the bull/bear gap is driven far more by **SG&A operating leverage and comp durability** than by unit count alone. In LOW, margins never inflect and EPS only reaches $1.16 by 2029 — the PE stays stranded at ~56x (expensive for a decelerating story = de-rating risk). In HIGH, margin maturation toward CAVA-style levels compounds EPS to $3.02, taking the PE to ~21x.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOW | 103 | 76 | 68 | 61 | 56 |
| BAU | 103 | 65 | 49 | 38 | 30 |
| HIGH | 103 | 59 | 40 | 29 | 21 |

### Scenario assumptions + justification

| Scenario | Shops/yr | SSS | EBITDA margin | Rate | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LOW | ~155–170 | +2% | flat 18% | 8% | Openings decelerate as East expansion cannibalises; consumer/gas headwind caps comps; no SG&A leverage; rates stay high on debt-funded builds |
| BAU | 190→235 | +4.5% | 18→21% | 6.5% | Guidance is ≥185 opens + 4–6% comps; SG&A leverages as base scales; ties to $2.05–2.08bn rev / $370–380m EBITDA guide |
| HIGH | 200→270 | +6.5% | 18→23.5% | 5% | Build machine accelerates; traffic-led comps sustain (7 straight quarters +ve transactions); margin approaches CAVA-style maturation; rates ease |

### External-factor sensitivity (2027E EPS, off BAU)

Oil is split into **direct** (demand/traffic) and **indirect** (cost) — both attributed to oil — so it isn't double-counted with genuinely non-oil inputs. Anchor: +100bps CoS/rev ≈ ‑8.2% EPS; ‑1.5pp SSS ≈ ‑6.8% EPS.

| Factor | Move | EPS impact | Channel |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Oil/gas — direct** | +$1/gal retail | **‑7%** | Drive-thru traffic falls, low-income guest pulls back (‑1.5pp SSS). Wingstop blamed gas for its Q1'26 comp miss |
| **Oil/gas — indirect** | same move | **‑5%** | Petrochemical packaging (cups/lids/straws) + diesel freight/distribution → ~+0.6pp CoS |
| **Oil/gas — TOTAL** | +$1/gal | **≈ ‑12%** | Direct + indirect stacked |
| Coffee + dairy (**non-oil**) | +100bps CoS/rev | ‑8% | Agricultural cycles (Brazil frost, feed/weather) — *not* oil-driven; the bulk of input cost sits here, so oil is a minority of input-cost risk |
| Wage inflation | +100bps CoS/rev | ‑8% | Shop labour; state minimum-wage moves |
| Rates — earnings | +100bps | ‑2.6% | Small; interest only ~2% of revenue |
| Rates — valuation | +100bps 10Y | *multiple* | Large; ~100x long-duration equity, ~15–20% de-rate risk |

**Note on oil vs input costs:** oil genuinely drives packaging and freight (the indirect channel above), but the two largest ingredient lines — coffee and dairy — move on their own supply cycles, so oil is *not* the majority of input-cost risk. Kept separate to avoid conflation.

**One-line justification:** priced for near-perfection at ~100x; BAU earnings drag the PE to ~30x by 2029 at a flat price, but LOW leaves it stranded at ~56x — that gap is the de-rating risk. The bull/bear swing is SG&A leverage + comps, not unit count. Rates barely touch earnings but dominate the multiple; oil is a double-hit (traffic + packaging/freight). No buy/sell call.
